findings.title: Blocked-email match statistics are rolled back when the block causes the save to fail
findings.body:
`BlockedEmail.should_block?` updates `match_count` and `last_match_at` from inside a validator. ActiveRecord runs `save` and `save!` validations inside the record's transaction, and when validation returns false the transaction is rolled back.

In the normal signup path (`user.save` in UsersController#create, `save!` in `create_for_email`), a `:block` match adds an error, the save fails, and the BlockedEmail update is rolled back. The statistics are never recorded for exactly the emails being blocked. Only `:do_nothing` matches, whose saves succeed, or the extra `user.valid?` call made outside a transaction when `call_discourse_hub?` is on, persist counts.

The specs don't catch this because they stub `should_block?` or call it directly, and transactional fixtures swallow the nested `ActiveRecord::Rollback`.

Fix: record the match outside the user's transaction (e.g. a separate connection or a job), or move the bookkeeping out of validation.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized, so blocks are trivially bypassed
findings.body:
`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact string comparison. `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` as typed, and neither the User model nor BlockedEmail downcases or strips the address.

If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up with `Bad@spammers.org` or `BAD@SPAMMERS.ORG` passes validation. Mail providers treat these as the same mailbox, so the blocking feature can be defeated with a single uppercase letter.

Fix: normalize with `Email.downcase(email).strip` both when storing BlockedEmail records and when querying, or use a case-insensitive comparison such as `lower(email) = ?`.

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment, also inflated by repeated validation calls
findings.body:
`record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write, so concurrent signup attempts with the same email lose increments.

Counts are also inflated because the check runs on every validation pass. UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save` when `call_discourse_hub?` is enabled. For `:do_nothing` emails both passes commit, so a single signup is counted twice.

Fix: use an atomic `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`, and avoid recording side effects from a validator that may run multiple times.

findings.title: Any server-side email error is shown inline as 'invalid email'
findings.body:
`rejectedEmails` is filled whenever the server returns any email error (line 274-275). That includes "has already been taken", the whitelist/blacklist "not allowed from that email provider", and the new "is not allowed".

The inline validation then always shows `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, which tells the user their address is malformed when it isn't. That is misleading and contradicts the flash message.

Fix: surface the server-provided reason, e.g. store `result.errors.email` alongside the rejected address and display it.

findings.title: New `errors`/`values` keys in the create response and the User/BlockedEmail integration are untested
findings.body:
The client now depends on `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` from the failed-signup JSON, but no controller spec asserts these keys are returned.

There is also no User model or controller spec showing that a BlockedEmail actually prevents account creation; the validator spec stubs `should_block?`. A regression in either the response shape or the `validates :email, email: true` wiring would go unnoticed.
